MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  July 10, 2018

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Sachs at 5:00 p.m., on July 10, 2018, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on July 5, 2018, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P.
Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Kelley
  Mayor Pro Tem Raths
  Mayor Sachs

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Real Property Negotiators: Government Code Section 54956.8:
  Property: APN#’s 856-061-30 and 856-061-40: Agency Negotiator– City Manager and
  City Attorney; Negotiating Parties – Mountain Star Development.

CS2. Conference with legal Counsel: Anticipated Litigation Initiation of Litigation
  Pursuant to Paragraph 4 of Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9 (1 case).

CS3. Conference with legal Counsel: Pending Litigation Pursuant to Paragraph 4 of
  Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9 - Southwest Voter Registration Education Project.

City Council Minutes  1  July 10, 2018
 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

Mayor Sachs recessed the meeting to Closed Session at 5:01 p.m. The City Council reconvened at
6:02 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council addressed three matters in Closed Session.
They received information and provided direction to staff but there was no reportable action.

INVOCATION: Council Member Goodell

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Bucknum

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Proclaim July 2018 To Be National Parks and Recreation Month

  Mayor Sachs presented the Proclamation to Mark Nix, Director of Recreation and
  Community Services.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

James Farris, M.V.: cited several concerns with the City‘s police services and asked if anyone has
considered an audit of the Sheriff’s Department.

Mary Grant, M.V.: on behalf of the American Cancer Society, she presented a plaque to thank
Mission Viejo for its many years of dedication to Relay for Life. She announced that the 2018
Relay for Life combined five cities’ efforts and raised more than $200,000.

Sherri George and Arabella Reyes, M.V.: stated that they represent the teachers and students of
Carl Hankey School and they wished to express their concern with school safety. They asked the
Council to support the idea of increasing peace officer presence on campuses during school hours
and proposed that deputies do their report-writing at local schools. The ladies noted that Carl
Hankey School has offered to pilot the program.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 7 and 8 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to approve
the Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  2  July 10, 2018
  1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of June 26, 2018, as presented.

2.  Check Register Dated June 15, 2018 in the Amount of $823,904.56

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Check Register Dated June 22, 2018 in the Amount of $747,357.04

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Highway Safety Improvement Program (HSIP) Call For Projects—Cycle 9—
  Citywide Installation of Audible Pedestrian Push Button Systems at Signalized
  Intersections

  (1) Adopted Resolution 18-31 Authorizing the Director of Public Works to Submit an
  Application for Highway Safety Improvement Program (HSIP) Grant Funds for the
  Citywide Installation of Audible Pedestrian Push Button Systems at Signalized
  Intersections; and (2) directed staff to transmit said Resolution to Caltrans by August 31,
  2018, in conjunction with the City's funding application for said project.

5.  Olympiad Road/Felipe Road Corridor Traffic Signal Synchronization Project (CIP
  18236)

  Awarded the construction contract in the amount of $357,100.00 to Elecnor Belco Electric,
  Inc., (A18- 16) for the subject project.

6.  Annual Weed Abatement Program for Parcels Under One Acre–Year 2018–Phase 1

  (1) Adopted Resolution 18-32 Declaring that Certain Weeds, Rubbish, Refuse, and Dirt on
  Parcels Under One Acre Constitute Nuisances; Declaring the Intention of the City Council
  to Order the Abatement of Said Nuisances; and Fixing a Time and Place for Hearing
  Protests; (2) instructed the Public Services Department to mail a Notice to Destroy Weeds
  in accordance with Section 39566 of the Government Code; and (3) instructed the City
  Clerk to set the Public Hearing for August 28, 2018.

9.  Comprehensive Bikeway and Transportation Connectivity Master Plan Consultant

  (1) Approved contract for the subject services to LSA (A18-17) for the period of July 1,
  2018 to July 31, 2019 in the amount of $99,900, and (2) authorized staff to issue a purchase
  order to LSA for the subject services.

10.  Carl Hankey School Safety Fence and Fence Fabrication and Installation Services at
  Various City Parks and Facilities

City Council Minutes  3  July 10, 2018
   (1) Approved first amendment for the subject services to the existing contract for J M Justus
  Fence Company in the amount of $19,736.00 for installation of Safety Fencing at Carl
  Hankey School and $15,000 for additional fencing fabrication and installation at various
  City parks and facilities; (2) authorized staff to issue a purchase order Change Order to J.
  M. Justus Fence Company for the subject services in an amount not to exceed $34,736.00;
  and (3) extended the contract terms through June 30, 2019.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

7.  2019 Orange County International Triathlon in Mission Viejo

  Council Member Bucknum noted that a few residents expressed concern with traffic flow
  issues during this year's event. She asked that those individuals be notified of next year’s
  planned street closures.

  Council Member Goodell agreed and said that the residents who complained should get a
  copy of the information in this agenda report now so they have advanced warning. He also
  suggested that all residents in the vicinity are notified earlier than the month of May 2019
  which was mentioned in the report.

  Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to
  approve the request submitted by Five Point Events to hold the 2019 Orange County
  International Triathlon in Mission Viejo on Sunday, June 2, 2019.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

8.  South Orange County Integrated Water Management Plan

  Council Member Goodell drew attention to the large document attached to agenda item 8.
  He said he has been attending Integrated Water Management Plan meetings and has learned
  quite a bit over the last year and a half. Council Member Goodell noted that he highlighted
  this item so those who are interested in water matters can look for it on the City’s website.

  Motion made by Council Member Goodell, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to adopt
  Resolution 18-33 Adopting the 2018 South Orange County Integrated Regional Water
  Management Plan.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  4  July 10, 2018
 OLD BUSINESS

11.  Revisions to City of Mission Viejo Personnel Policies

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to
  adopt Resolution 18-34 Providing for the Revisions to Select Personnel Policies.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

NEW BUSINESS

12.  Amending the City of Mission Viejo Salary Schedule and Authorized Position
  Schedule

  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services, presented the staff report and Director
  of Information Technology Jackie Alexander answered the City Council Member’s
  questions.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to adopt
  Resolution 18-34 Providing for the Revisions to Select Personnel Policies.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

13.  Annual Performance Evaluation of the City Manager

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Sachs, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to adopt Resolution
  18-36 Approving Certain Compensation of the City Manager.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  5  July 10, 2018
 MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

14.  Orange County Local Agency Formation Commission (LAFCO) Report

  Council Member Bucknum presented the report.

15.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Mayor Sachs presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

16.  Orange County Sheriff’s Department (OCSD) Update from Chief Vuong

  Chief Vuong outlined upcoming Sheriff’s Department events and training sessions and
  announced that School Resource Officer (SRO) Deputy Timmins is taking another position
  with the department so the SRO role will transition to Deputy Duran. He thanked the teacher
  and student who spoke earlier in the evening about school safety. Chief Vuong noted that the
  Orange County Sheriff’s Department is planning to give the proposal a try and Mission
  Viejo’s Quality of Life Deputy will begin deploying from Carl Hankey school for the "Adopt
  a Cop" pilot program.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

17. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum thanked the student and scouts in the audience who stayed for the
entire City Council Meeting. She outlined recent events including Quail Run neighborhood’s
Independence Day parade and the 4th of July Street Faire and Fireworks Spectacular. She thanked
the Mission Viejo Lake Association, Police Services personnel, the Mission Viejo Activities
Committee and City staff for making the terrific event happen annually. Council Member
Bucknum also mentioned her recent attendance at the Orange County Forum luncheon where she
received regional updates. She reminded residents of the upcoming Concert in the Park with the
band Family Style on July 27 and the “Totally 80s” celebration of Mission Viejo’s 30th
anniversary at the Prelude in the Park and Pacific Symphony event on July 28. Council Member
Bucknum encouraged residents to take the shuttle to and from civic center or ride their bikes to
the events. In closing, she announced that on August 8 the Orange County Fair will celebrate
“Mission Viejo Day” with a special flag raising at 12:30 p.m. to honor the City.

City Council Minutes  6  July 10, 2018
 Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell announced that the Chamber of Commerce State of the City breakfast
was great and he really enjoyed Planning Commissioner Bob Breton’s excellent overview of the
history of the brand of Mission Viejo from the ranch days through present times. Council Member
Goodell noted that there will be another big swim meet at the Marguerite Aquatics Complex,
August 10-12, with the regional Southwest Zone Summer Championships for Masters Swimmers.
He hinted that attendees might even see a City Council Member (himself) swimming.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley thanked the dedicated volunteers of the Mission Viejo Activities
Committee who plan the 4th of July Street Faire every year. She attended again last week and said
it is a wonderful celebration put on by a small number of people but it benefits thousands. She
encouraged residents to sign up to serve on the Activities Committee and she thanked City
Commissioners Cathy Allen and Pam Smith who had a big part in the planning of this year’s event.
Council Member Kelley discussed Mission Viejo Library’s Summer Reading program which her
grandchildren are participating in and said it’s a wonderful way to encourage reading. The program
is free and there are weekend events included in the schedule. She discussed her attendance at the
Senior Corps of Retirees (SCOR) recognition event earlier in the day. The Sheriff’s Department
has a group of seniors who provide services to the City such as vacation home checks,
neighborhood patrols, volunteering at the front desk, and a variety of other things. She said she
appreciated the opportunity to attend the meeting to thank those volunteers for providing a service
that saves the City a lot of money. Council Member Kelley announced that on Sunday, July 22 the
Mission Viejo Marine Adoption Committee will host Boots, Beer and Barbecue to benefit the
City’s adopted Headquarters Battalion Marines from Camp Pendleton. The event is from 4:00 to
7:00 p.m. at the Murray Community Center and tickets can be purchased ahead of time for $25 per
person which includes food catered by Outback restaurant, along with line dancing and other
activities. She noted that her son had some items stolen from his truck while it was parked in her
driveway so she reminded residents to lock their cars. Council Member Kelley recapped the
Mission Viejo Community of Character program and noted that the character quality for the month
of July is fairness. In closing, she shared a quote by Michael Josephson: “A person of character
plays fair even when others don’t and values no achievement unless it was attained with honor.”

Mayor Pro Tem Raths

Mayor Pro Tem Raths announced that he was nominated by Supervisor Lisa Bartlett to serve on
the Orange County Veterans Advisory Council and last month he was elected as the Vice
Chairman. The Advisory Council has asked the Orange County Board of Supervisors to look at
options for locating a veteran’s cemetery somewhere in Orange County and he thanked the Board
for looking after veterans by conducting a study on possible locations. Mayor Pro Tem Raths
announced that tomorrow morning he will be the guest speaker at the Rotary Club meeting which
will be held at Mission Viejo Country Club beginning at 7:10 a.m.

City Council Minutes  7  July 10, 2018
 Mayor Sachs

Mayor Sachs congratulated the teacher and student from Carl Hankey School that came out for the
meeting tonight to seek information on school safety. He noted that Secure OC Schools has
received a lot of input from students and recently, he and Chief Vuong walked around Newhart
School with a Scout who is interested in safety measures too. Mayor Sachs said he is impressed
with the students who are becoming engaged and active in identifying situations and other students
who might be a threat. Between School Resource Officers, psychologists, teachers and
administrators, he said schools across the country are starting to get a better handle on safety and
identifying considerations. Mayor Sachs stated that one of the heart-wrenching things he has
learned is that suicides are starting to go all the way down into elementary school children and
there are a lot of things that adults are not aware of so students are taking it upon themselves to
make sure that their friends are taken care. In conclusion, Mayor Sachs provided an update on his
goals for the second quarter of 2018.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 7:45 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Sachs adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, August 28, 2018, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of August 28, 2018

City Council Minutes  8  July 10, 2018
